examples.title: The AI map of the Algarve, by town and kind
examples.about: How many organisations each place's agent has mapped, by kind.
examples.sql:
SELECT p.name AS place, m.kind, count(*) AS entries
FROM map m JOIN places p ON p.id = m.place
GROUP BY p.name, m.kind
ORDER BY entries DESC, place
LIMIT 20

examples.title: Who is on more than one town's AI map
examples.about: Connecting the dots: the organisations that several place agents found on their own, merged by name.
examples.sql:
SELECT n.label AS organisation, n.kind, count(DISTINCT e.dst) AS towns,
       group_concat(DISTINCT replace(e.dst, 'place:', '')) AS places
FROM edges e JOIN nodes n ON n.id = e.src
WHERE e.verb = 'on_ai_map_of'
GROUP BY n.id
HAVING towns > 1
ORDER BY towns DESC, organisation

examples.title: What the detectives connected, and how sure they are
examples.about: detective.places@'s links, each end resolved to a node of the graph; 'read' means the page itself was opened, 'search_extract' only a search result.
examples.sql:
SELECT a.label AS from_node, c.verb, b.label AS to_node, c.verified, c.places
FROM connections c
JOIN nodes a ON a.id = c.src
JOIN nodes b ON b.id = c.dst
ORDER BY c.verified, a.label

examples.title: Every company and organisation within two steps of the Universidade do Algarve, through the stories
examples.about: A graph traversal inside SQL: neighbours(start, depth, verbs) walks the edges both ways. Through mentions, two steps is "named in the same story": the university, a story that names it, and who else that story names.
examples.sql:
SELECT n.depth, n.label, n.type, n.path
FROM neighbours((SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE label LIKE 'Universidade do Algarve%' ORDER BY id LIMIT 1), 2, 'mentions') n
WHERE n.type IN ('company', 'organisation') AND n.depth > 0
ORDER BY n.depth, n.label
LIMIT 40

examples.title: How Loulé connects to Faro, not counting the region
examples.about: paths(from, to, max_depth, verbs) finds the shortest paths; '-located_in' skips the trivial path through the Algarve.
examples.sql:
SELECT hops, path, verbs
FROM paths('place:loule', 'place:faro', 4, '-located_in')
LIMIT 10

examples.title: The newest local AI stories, and how far each is from AI
examples.about: Every story carries its source, the day it was read and its path to AI (steps 0 is about AI directly).
examples.sql:
SELECT date, place, title, publisher, steps, ai_path
FROM news
ORDER BY date DESC
LIMIT 15

examples.title: Which stories name an organisation on the map
examples.about: The mentions edges join a story to the organisations whose names are in its headline or summary.
examples.sql:
SELECT s.label AS story, o.label AS names, group_concat(DISTINCT replace(r.dst, 'place:', '')) AS reported_in
FROM edges m
JOIN nodes s ON s.id = m.src AND s.type = 'news'
JOIN nodes o ON o.id = m.dst
JOIN edges r ON r.src = s.id AND r.verb = 'reported_in'
WHERE m.verb = 'mentions'
GROUP BY s.id, o.id
ORDER BY o.label
LIMIT 25

examples.title: What the places rest on: the sources by web host
examples.about: Every story and map entry by the host of its source: a newsroom's dependency on a few outlets, in one query.
examples.sql:
SELECT host, count(*) AS items, count(DISTINCT place) AS places
FROM (SELECT place, host FROM news UNION ALL SELECT place, host FROM map) x
WHERE host IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY host
ORDER BY items DESC
LIMIT 15

examples.title: How fresh each place is
examples.about: When each place's items were read, and its status.
examples.sql:
SELECT p.name, p.status, p.updated, p.news, p.map, p.gaps,
       (SELECT max(read_on) FROM map WHERE place = p.id) AS map_read
FROM places p
ORDER BY p.news + p.map DESC

examples.title: The shape of the whole graph
examples.about: Nodes by type and layer: the shared graph and the by-place layer in one id space.
examples.sql:
SELECT layer, type, count(*) AS nodes
FROM nodes
GROUP BY layer, type
ORDER BY layer, nodes DESC

examples.title: Which sources are captured, and their hashes
examples.about: Every cited page and its capture: join the stories to the captures by URL to see what each story rests on, and the SHA-256 that proves what the page said when it was read.
examples.sql:
SELECT n.place, n.title, c.host, c.captured_at, substr(c.image_sha256, 1, 16) AS image_sha256
FROM news n JOIN captures c ON c.url = n.url
WHERE c.ok = 1
ORDER BY n.place, n.date DESC

place_examples.title: {name}'s AI map, with the path to AI
place_examples.about: Each entry, its kind, its source's host and the day it was read.
place_examples.sql:
SELECT name, kind, steps, ai_path, host, read_on
FROM map
WHERE place = '{place}'
ORDER BY steps, name

place_examples.title: {name}'s local AI stories
place_examples.about: Newest first, with the publisher and the path to AI.
place_examples.sql:
SELECT date, title, publisher, steps, ai_path
FROM news
WHERE place = '{place}'
ORDER BY date DESC

place_examples.title: Everything within two steps of {name}
place_examples.about: A traversal from the place's node; the path shows how each is reached.
place_examples.sql:
SELECT depth, type, label, path
FROM neighbours('place:{place}', 2, '-located_in')
WHERE depth > 0 AND type NOT IN ('source', 'fact', 'evidence')
ORDER BY depth, type, label
LIMIT 40

place_examples.title: Who on {name}'s map is also on another place's map
place_examples.about: The organisations this place shares with the rest of the Algarve.
place_examples.sql:
SELECT n.label, group_concat(DISTINCT replace(e2.dst, 'place:', '')) AS also_in
FROM edges e1
JOIN nodes n ON n.id = e1.src
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.src = e1.src AND e2.verb = 'on_ai_map_of' AND e2.dst != 'place:{place}'
WHERE e1.verb = 'on_ai_map_of' AND e1.dst = 'place:{place}'
GROUP BY n.id
ORDER BY n.label

place_examples.title: What {name}'s page rests on
place_examples.about: The sources its agent reads, and how many of its items rest on each host.
place_examples.sql:
SELECT name, kind, host, items
FROM sources
WHERE place = '{place}'
ORDER BY items DESC, name

place_examples.title: What {name}'s agent has not found yet
place_examples.about: The gaps, in the agent's words.
place_examples.sql: SELECT n, text FROM gaps WHERE place = '{place}' ORDER BY n
